title: Technical Objection Handling — Developer Platform Buyers (deck sketch)
content:
Purpose: quick slide deck + speaker notes for SDR/AE/SE to handle technical objections from platform/infra engineers evaluating DIY inference vs Redwood Inference. Draft — thrown together after 2 calls with Platform buyer prospects.

Deck outline (sketch):

Slide 0 — Title + framing
Title: "Technical Tradeoffs: DIY Inference vs Redwood Inference"
Subhead: short, developer-first rebut frameworks for platform engineers
Speaker note: set tone: we respect DIY. This is about pragmatic tradeoffs (cost, ops burden, latency, reliability, security controls).

Slide 1 — Quick hypothesis map (1 slide)
Bullet points:
- When teams say "we can build it ourselves" they usually underestimate ops complexity (cache consistency, KV cache, long-tail latency).
- Primary buyer concerns: data control, latency SLOs, unit economics, multi-model upgrades, security/compliance.
- Our lever: predictable serving runtime + deployment abstraction + routing/fallbacks.
Speaker note: use real customer anecdote (healthcare med-ML) — they tested DIY for 6 months, then moved to Dedicated for predictable latency during peak hours.

Slide 2 — Top 5 technical objections and short counters (one-liners + 1 slide each to expand)
- "We already have Kubernetes + Triton": Counter: Infrastructure doesn't remove model-serving semantics — LRU/kv cache, prefix caching, efficient KV eviction require careful runtime tie-ins; Triton helps but doesn't implement routing, quality-aware fallbacks or inference-aware compilation choices.
- "Cost — we can be cheaper hosting ourselves": Counter: question unit economics across engineering time, MTTR for incidents, and long-tail percentiles; include example TCO table (sample numbers below).
- "We need private / VPC on-prem for compliance": Counter: Redwood Private + VPC options provide customer-controlled control-plane + KMS integrations; reduces build vs buy verification effort.
- "We can't trust an external API for PII workloads": Counter: show auditing, optional private control plane, and per-request encryption hooks.
- "Latency requirements <50ms p95": Counter: show how routing policies, dedicated pools, and KV caching reduce cold-starts and tail latency.

Speaker note: expand each objection into demoable artefact (traces, p95 charts, SLA docs).

Slide 3 — Example TCO comparison (engineer-hours + infra) — high-level table (sketch)
- Rows: Initial build (weeks), ongoing ops (FTEs), infra cost (monthly), reliability risk multiplier, security validation effort.
- Example numbers (placeholder):
  - DIY: build 12 weeks, 2.5 FTE ongoing, infra $18k/mo, compliance time +2 months, risk multiplier 1.8
  - Redwood Dedicated: onboard 2 weeks, 0.3 FTE ongoing, infra $25k/mo (reserved + SLA), compliance time +1 week, risk multiplier 1.05
Speaker note: emphasize that infra cost alone is not the whole story — FTE burden and time-to-fix matter. Add link to internal TCO workbook (TODO: attach).

Slide 4 — Tactical demo checklist for SEs (what to show in 20–30 minutes)
- Show p95 tail for chat generation: DIY vs Redwood on same model (or same quantized variant)
- Show failing scenario + automatic fallback to compatible cheaper variant (routing policy demo)
- Show caching: prefix reuse saving tokens & latency (before/after traces)
- Show rollout policy: canary -> full -> instant rollback + metrics (console screenshots)
- Show cost/latency heatmap and token-level breakdown in Console
Speaker note: each demo should be reproducible; keep a short script under 30 minutes. Link to runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/SE-DEMO-RUNBOOK (placeholder)

Slide 5 — Conversation scripts (SE / AE quick bullets)
- When buyer says: "we can host cheaper": "Totally — can I show you where engineers spend time after launch? We track incidents, patch cycles, and tuning time — in many cases the run-rate cost of ops + incidents exceeds infra delta within 6–9 months."
- When buyer says: "we need full control of keys/data": "We support customer-managed KMS and private control plane — let's walk through the audit logs and KMS integration in our private deployment spec."
- When buyer says: "we already use X inference runtime": "Great — where do you observe tail latency, and how do you handle fallbacks when a pod fails? We can integrate with existing runtimes or replace the runtime gradually with our optimized kernels."

Speaker note: include short code snippet for showing IAM + KMS snippet in onboarding (insert later).

Slide 6 — Risk-first FAQ (detailed answers to ask during discovery)
- Q: "How do you handle model updates without breaking production?" A: rollout policies, shadowing, per-prompt evaluation hooks, automatic quality regression alerts tied to evals.
- Q: "How are KV caches consistent across shards?" A: runtime-level KV cache with TTL, deterministic shard placement, and optional sticky routing — we provide audit hooks in tracing.
- Q: "What about GPU resource fragmentation?" A: dedicated pools and automatic packing; when fragmentation hurts throughput we fallback to spare capacity or compatible model variants.

Slide 7 — Engineering appendix (deeper details SEs can pull up if needed)
- Short notes on kernel selection heuristics, quantization profiles, and batching strategies.
- Link to internal perf benchmarks: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/serving-runtime-perf (placeholder)

Appendix / extra materials (notes to self):
- Pull concrete numbers from perf team: p50/p95 improvements by model family (LLAMA2-13B, MPT-7B, mix) — ticket: JIRA-2456 (perf data request).
- Prepare one-sheeter comparing SLO/SLIs between Hosted vs DIY vs Dedicated.
- Add customer quote: "We kept p95 under 120ms during Black Friday using Redwood routing + cache" — ask CS for permission to use.
- TODO: add security checklist for regulated verticals (finance, healthcare) — link to security-and-compliance page.

Tone and format guidance:
- Keep slides concise, data-driven, and engineer-respectful. Avoid marketing fluff.
- Include quick-run commands and console screenshots for SEs to show live.
- Flag any claims that need legal/security signoff before use in external-facing decks.

Open questions (for product/engineering to answer before turning to final):
- Exact numbers for TCO model (need real FTE per-customer baselines). Contact: Jordan Lee (solutions eng) and Perf team.
- Can we reveal kernel/quantization benchmarks publicly or only in NDA contexts? Check with Security & Legal.
- Are there prebuilt demo environments (sandbox org) for Dedicated flows? If not, create one.

Meeting log / provenance:
- Origins: synthesized from calls with Platform buyers (2025-10) and internal AE/SE postmortem notes (Q3 wins/losses).
- This is intentionally rough — aim to workshop with SEs in the next enablement session (suggested date: 2026-02-28).

Speaker closing line (script): "We built Redwood so you don't have to rebuild the whole inference stack; instead you get predictable economics, fewer outages, and controlled upgrades. If you'd like, we can map a 30-day technical evaluation plan against your current stack — here's how a 2-week POC looks..."

Misc: save drafts as small slide deck + separate cheat sheet for SDRs. This file is the master sketch — please add notes inline rather than making new files.
